caption: The drawing consists of a square composition bordered by a thick, black-outlined frame, which is decorated with alternating vertical sections of pale green and cream color, as well as curved maroon and red shapes along the left and right sides. Inside the frame, the background is primarily filled with a light, muted pink. At the top of the inner square is a pair of red and white drapery elements, curved in a scalloped pattern. Centrally positioned is a large, black cross with wide, flat ends. Overlapping the cross are two stylized, disembodied human arms reaching toward one another. The left arm, extending from the left edge, is bare and colored off-white with red accent lines; it is bisected with a red edge near the shoulder. The right arm, extending from the right edge, is also off-white and is draped in blue fabric, with a circular arrangement of greenish-yellow shapes with dark centers (possibly a crown of thorns or a wreath) encircling the wrist. Near the lower left corner of the inner panel, there is a small object resembling three brown nails arranged in a tripod shape. The bottom of the frame displays vertical red and white stripes. The overall color palette includes cream, maroon, red, olive green, blue, black, off-white, and yellowish-green. The number "14" appears in small blue text in the lower left corner outside the main frame.
title: Plate 14: Main Altarpiece, Chimayo: From Portfolio "Spanish Colonial Designs of New Mexico"
